items.title: Dollar hits fresh 18-month high as hot inflation boosts Fed hike expectation
items.excerpt: The U.S. dollar hit an 18-month high on Wednesday after stronger-than-expected inflation ​data revived expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike later this month, highlighting concern that price pressures are broadening across ‌the economy. The Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Wednesday that U.S. consumer prices rose sharply in September as gasoline costs surged. "The higher-than-expected core inflation print raises concerns that energy-driven inflation is spreading to other areas of the economy," said Uto Shinohara, senior investment strategist at Mesirow Currency Management. ... The U.S. ​dollar index, a measure of the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, rose 0.38% to 102.57. The index earlier hit its highest since April 2025, ​shaking off the previous day's losses. ... On Thursday, Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman also signaled a wait-and-see approach before raising ​rates again. ... Traders now see a 67% chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, compared with 53% a month ago, while ​pricing in about 79 basis points of tightening by late 2027, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed ...
